evidence.quote: a complete smooth metric $g$ on $\mathbb R^n$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_g\geq0$

outputs.exact_statement:
There are an even integer $n\geq8$, an integer $k\geq2$, and a complete smooth metric $g$ on $\mathbb R^n$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_g\geq0$ and $$h_k(\mathbb R^n,g)>h_k(\mathbb R^n,g_{\mathrm E}).$$ The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its asymptotic volume ratio satisfies $$0<\lim_{R\to\infty}
 \frac{\operatorname{vol}_g B_g(0,R)}{\omega_nR^n}<1,$$ where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball.

For all sufficiently large odd $m$, $$\label{eq:weighted-quantile-gap}
 (m-1)\mathcal J_m>2.$$

There is an odd $m=2s-1\ge7$ for which the following choices are possible. The parameters $a_*\in(0,1)$ and $q_*>1$ can be taken arbitrarily close to $1$, with [eq:link-margin] holding at $a=a_*$ for every $q\in[1,q_*]$. For these parameters there are integers $k\ge2$, $L\ge2$, and $0\le M_l\le N_l$ for $2\le l\le L$ such that, on abbreviating $d_{l,i}=d_{l,i}(a_*,q_*)$, $$\label{eq:selection} \overline d_l:=\frac1{M_l}\sum_{i=1}^{M_l}d_{l,i}0, \qquad \sum_{l=2}^L M_l>\sum_{l=0}^k N_l.$$

Fix positive numbers $\kappa_l$, $2\leq l\leq L$. As $J$ ranges over all orthogonal complex structures on $\mathbb R^{2s}$, the tuples $$X_J=\bigl(\kappa_l(D_J^2|_{V_l})_{\mathrm{tf}}\bigr)_{l=2}^L
 \label{eq:control-generators}$$ generate, under real linear combinations and brackets, the full Lie algebra $$\bigoplus_{l=2}^L\mathfrak{sl}(V_l).$$

Let $d=\sum_{l=2}^L(N_l^2-1)$. There exist finitely many orthogonal complex structures $J_1,\ldots,J_R$, an open neighborhood $U$ of zero in $\mathbb R^d$, and smooth real functions $c_1,\ldots,c_R$ on $U$ such that $$\mathcal W(h)=
   \exp(c_R(h)X_{J_R})\cdots\exp(c_1(h)X_{J_1})$$ satisfies $\mathcal W(0)=\Pi$, and $$D\mathcal W(0):\mathbb R^d\longrightarrow T_\Pi\mathcal G$$ is an isomorphism. The same assertion holds for any prescribed target in $\mathcal G$.

For the fixed spectral data above, there are a smooth function $a:\mathbb R\to(0,1]$ and an index $j_{\rm geom}$ such that, for every $j_0\geq j_{\rm geom}$, every sequence $(h_j)_{j\geq j_0}$ in $K$, used in the preceding scheme, defines a smooth complete metric on $\mathbb R^{m+1}$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature: $$g=dr^2+r^2\gamma(\log r),\qquad
 \gamma(t)=G(a(t),q(t),J(t)).$$ The function $a$ is identically $1$ for $t\leq2$, decreases to $a_*$, and, for some $\mu>0$, satisfies $$\label{eq:scale-tail}
 b(t):=\frac{a'(t)}{a(t)}
       =-\mu(1+t)^{-5/4}\quad(t\geq4),
 \qquad
 \log\frac{a(t)}{a_*}=4\mu(1+t)^{-1/4}\quad(t\geq4).$$ The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its distance from the origin is exactly $r$. Its volume form is $$d\operatorname{vol}_g
   =r^m a(\log r)^m\,dr\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_0}.$$ The function $a$ and the starting index $j_0$ can be chosen independently of the sequence of control parameters.

There are a threshold $j_{\rm reg}\geq j_{\rm geom}$ and constants $0[eq:harmonic-ode]. Their value vector at any one time can be prescribed arbitrarily and determines the solution uniquely. At each pulse start one also has $$\|P_l(t_j)-\theta_l I\|\leq Cj^{-2} \qquad(j\geq j_0), \label{eq:round-reset}$$ including the first pulse. The constants and the threshold are uniform over all preceding choices of the parameters in $K$.

The matrices $U_{l,j}$, $V_{l,j}$, and $D_{l,j}$ have positive diagonal entries, and $$0\leq K_{l,j}\leq\theta_l^{-1}I.
 \label{eq:K-bound}$$ They depend only on the prescribed diagonal leg, not on its current or earlier pulse parameters. The exact transmission identity is $$D_{l,j}^{-1}\mathcal T_{l,j}(h)
 =\left[I+K_{l,j}\bigl(P_{l,e}(h)-\theta_lI\bigr)\right]
       \mathcal B_{l,j}(h).
 \label{eq:full-normalization}$$ Moreover, uniformly for the finite set of $l,i$, $$\log (D_{l,j})_{ii}
 =L_jd_{l,i}+O(1+L_jj^{-2}+T_j)
 =L_j\bigl(d_{l,i}+o(1)\bigr).
 \label{eq:diagonal-growth}$$

For finite spectral data as specified at the end of Section 3, choose the word and compact pulse family above. There are a starting index $j_0$ and parameters $h_j\in K$, for every $j\geq j_0$, such that the center-regular value transmissions of the resulting metric satisfy $$\mathcal T_{l,j}=s_{l,j}D_{l,j}\Pi_l,\qquad s_{l,j}>0,\qquad |\log s_{l,j}|\leq C T_j \quad(2\leq l\leq L,\ j\geq j_0). \label{eq:exact-transmission}$$ The positive diagonal matrices $D_{l,j}$ propagate the reference Cauchy data $(I,\theta_l I)$ over the entire leg following the pulse; they satisfy [eq:diagonal-growth]. The regular value equation has the bounds [eq:riccati-barriers]. All estimates used to choose $j_0$ are uniform over preceding admitted controls for this fixed finite family.

Let $g$ be the metric constructed in the proof of Theorem 1, with link parameters $a_*,q_*$ and comparison integer $k$. Every cone with link $G(a_*,q,J_0)$, $1\leq q\leq q_*$, occurs as a pointed tangent cone at infinity. In particular the tangent cone is not unique. The metric $g$ is not locally conformally flat. If $\mathcal D(M)$ denotes the union of nonnegative homogeneous harmonic degrees over all its tangent cones, then $\mathcal D(M)$ contains a half-line and a neighborhood of $k$.
